articles.content: Workforce Skilling & Upskilling the Workforce: AI Innovation & Research, Emerging Founders Program, AI for the Navy Navanwita Bora Sachdev - November 16, 2026 SHARE The Tech Panda takes a look at the efforts at skilling, upskilling, and reskilling in the tech industry. ValuePitch & SMVIT Strengthen Partnership with Centre for Advanced AI Innovation & Research to Build India’s Next Generation of AI Innovators ValuePitch, an AI and Decision Intelligence company, has strengthened its long-standing partnership with Sir M. Visvesvaraya Institute of Technology (SMVIT) through the establishment of the Centre for Advanced AI Innovation & Research, a dedicated hub designed to bridge the gap between academia and industry by enabling students to work on real-world AI challenges. The partnership builds on a relationship that began in 2018 with a sponsored research project and has since evolved into one of ValuePitch’s flagship industry-academia initiatives. Ntheye X SMVIT Venkat Ramana, CEO, ValuePitch & NthEye, said, “India has no shortage of engineering talent. What students often lack is the opportunity to work on real-world problems that challenge them to think beyond the classroom. Our partnership with SMVIT is built on the belief that innovation happens when academia and industry work together, giving young innovators access to live technologies, experienced mentors, and the freedom to experiment. Through the Centre for Advanced AI Innovation & Research, we want to nurture not just future AI professionals, but future builders, researchers, and entrepreneurs who can create globally relevant solutions from India.” VenturEdu Launches Emerging Founders Program, Offers Up to Rs 50,000 Stipend to Young Entrepreneurs at 2-Day Bootcamp VenturEdu, India’s first residential venture-building programme for aspiring founders, has launched the Emerging Founders Program, a zero-fee initiative for young entrepreneurs aged 18 to 28 to take early-stage ideas through an intensive venture-building process. “Young people today are increasingly willing to consider entrepreneurship early in their careers, but an idea at 20 or 25 is rarely accompanied by the network, operating experience or access to capital needed to build a company. The Emerging Founders Program is designed to bridge that gap by giving young founders a structured environment to test an idea, build a product and learn directly from people who have built and scaled businesses,” said Kulmani Rana, Founder, VenturEdu. BIMTECH Strengthens AI Innovation Ecosystem with Inauguration of Centre of Excellence on AI Rooted in experiential learning and innovation, Birla Institute of Management Technology (BIMTECH), an AACSB-accredited business school in India, successfully inaugurated its Centre of Excellence on AI on yesterday, marking a significant step in strengthening the institute’s focus on artificial intelligence, experiential learning, innovation and technology-driven education. The inauguration of the AI Centre of Excellence brought together 400+ participants, primarily students and faculty members, under the vision Learn. Build. Deploy. Innovate. articles.title: Cold Calling: Film chronicles how scientists braved extreme conditions to build India's first ...
articles.content: Braving the icy desert of Antarctica, around 43 years ago, a team of 81 Indian scientists, Army, Navy and Air Force personnel achieved something that had never been done before or since then: building a permanent research station in one Antarctic summer, a period of six months. “No country, including the US, Russia or China, had achieved what these guys were proposing on this trip. Permanent stations used to be built little by little over years, but there are multiple problems with that; it’s inefficient and sometimes, the previous years’ gets undone because of the ice. So it was an onerous task and they were given only a 15 per cent chance of success by experts. But they prevailed against all odds,” says filmmaker Santosh Saligram. He and collaborator Sourabha Rao, screened their documentary Miracle in Antarctica chronicling this historic feat in Indian science history, at BLR Design Centre, Church Street, on Sunday. The station, built the same year as India signed the Antarctic Treaty, was India’s third expedition to the continent and was crucial because a permanent research station meant that Indian scientists could stay to continue their research throughout the inhospitable winter months. “Twelve nations had already signed the Antarctic Treaty which denounced any activity in Antarctica other than science and research. India wanted to be taken seriously in its capabilities in science and research, and share international space in the Antarctic discussion,” explains Saligram. At the core of the documentary are interviews with three scientists: Harsh Kumar Gupta who led the mission, KJ Mathew and Ashok Hanjura, along with a few conversations with their family and friends, helping paint a picture of the people at the core of the mission. This was important to the duo since the project was born out of Gupta’s search for someone to do justice to the story, after being put off by Bollywood sensationalism, notes Rao, adding, “One part of the story is the science but the other is the scientists as people.” Avoiding sensationalism doesn’t mean the story of the expedition has any dearth of excitement though, with Saligram sharing that one incident that kept resurfacing across interviews was a close brush with death soon after the scientists’ ship reached the Antarctic ice wall. “M18 helicopters were being used to transport cargo inland from the ship. On the third day, the helicopter crashed into the water and the five people inside had to break the plexiglass window at the bottom to escape,” he says, continuing, “While being rescued by a second helicopter, two people caught hold of the rope but did not sling it properly. Because their hands must have been freezing, they fell into the water again from a great height. You can actually see this in the footage in the documentary. It’s utterly terrifying.
